findings.reason: the plan already carries this as §61 with the owner named (`reckon/service.py`) and the remedy stated (one resolver, one installer), so the review confirms rather than changes it.
findings.text: `SystemdUserWatchService` reimplements `reckon/service.py`'s `unit_path`/`installed`/`write_unit` and hardcodes `~/.config/systemd/user`, while `paid_lanes.systemd_user_dir()` (`reckon/crew/paid_lanes.py:750`) resolves `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` the way the manager does, so three sites disagree and a unit can be written where systemd never reads it

findings.reason: §22 must name the owner that `check-manifest` reuses rather than add a third resolver, or the citation check forks and the two existing copies drift as they already have.
findings.text: `_commit_resolves_in` is defined a second time here, duplicating `reckon/crew/promotion.py:477` (which delegates to `_commit_canonical_id`), and §22 proposes adding a third commit-resolution path inside `reckon/cli.py`'s `check-manifest` (which today resolves no commit)

findings.reason: §16 measured this pair directly and chose to keep two readers with the differing return shapes stated (tri-state for the row, boolean for the sweep); the finding is recorded, not a change.
findings.text: a second wait-condition probe `_run_condition_probe` duplicates `reckon/crew/recovery.py`'s `_run_wait_condition_probe`, which §16 measured as "a contract with two readers"

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan hides behaviour behind narrow interfaces rather than spreading it: `check_serving_origin` returns one receipt dict hiding launcher query + timeout + HTTP probe; §61 consolidates the watcher service onto one resolver and one installer (`reckon/service.py`) parameterised by unit name; the rest extend an existing reader with one added guard.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — two concrete forked mechanisms remain: the watcher service reimplements `reckon/service.py`, and `_commit_resolves_in` is defined twice (promotion and reports) while §22 proposes a third commit-resolution path in `check-manifest`.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan searches and cites the mechanism it extends at every new-machinery node: §3 names `watcher_state` in `reckon/crew/runs.py`; §4 names the wait reader in `reckon/crew/recovery.py`; §6 names the four repository-resolving surfaces (`dispatch.py`, `resumption.py`, `ledger.py`, `promotion.py`); §13 records `reckon/flight.py`'s endpoint reader (`_probe_serving`, `reckon/flight.py:1518`) as prior art before adding `serving_origin.py`; §16 names both probe readers; §61 names `reckon/service.py:unit_path` and `paid_lanes.systemd_user_dir()`.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the only wrapping proposed is justified where it appears: §61 routes `SystemdUserWatchService` through `reckon/service.py` rather than copying it, and §13 adds a new module only after §13's own prior-art note shows `flight.py` compares the document to the configured model and not to the resolved launcher; §10 reuses `reckon.crew.dispatch`'s producer rather than authoring a second one.
